propositions: Source comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that decay over time, with 8+ cited SHAs already unreachable in the current tree

A new static-analysis detector identifies rot-prone comment patterns (SHA-like hex >=7 chars, run/job/thread IDs >=8 digits, date tokens paired with past-tense incident verbs) and must be integrated as a CI gate to prevent future violations

Detector acceptor must correctly distinguish valid tickets/epics/stories (hex 4x4 ids or word-triple aliases) and escape-hatch 'context: external' refs from false positives (e.g., 'bug surfaced' phrasing or path names matching alias pattern)
All detector hits at HEAD must be remediated by deleting rot-prone tokens, citing a resolvable ticket, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log
The delivered guard implementation contained a false-accept bug where the word-triple-alias pattern matched hyphenated file paths, causing two sites to be incorrectly skipped during remediation sweep
The detector's own unit test module must self-exclude via EXCLUDED_FILES tuple to permit test fixtures containing live rot-prone tokens without in-tree escape-hatch suppressions
